//: Story Phase 5, chapter 23: Dressed for Disaster. Afternoon. A shark impact to starboard, and the Grand Stenchmaster's chair is empty: the crew think he has finally gone to help. He's in the cargo hold, behind the crates, with a needle and a tablecloth. Back on deck: the self-important fanfare, THE GRAND STENCHMASTER SUIT (the sash is part of it now), the tour (sash, epaulettes, medals, coat, boots), the crew, Jim's tablecloth, the captain, 'every Grand Stenchmaster', the order to help, the refusal (it's formalwear), and three starboard patches while he stands about being motivational.
p5c4.begin: WHUMP. This time it's the starboard side. A whole length of rail sags outward with a groan.
jory[alarmed]: Starboard's taking bites now, Captain! Three of 'em, low down!
gristle: Right. Everybody grab a— hang on.
Everyone looks at the station. The S.E.S. is on, playing to nobody: a fish, going round and round. The chair is empty. The grog mug is empty. The Grand Stenchmaster is nowhere.
pete[happy]: He's gone to HELP. He's finally gone to help!
pete: Well, he took a hammer.
jim[annoyed]: He took a TABLECLOTH. I saw him. And me good scissors.
A thoughtful silence falls, which is a thing that almost never happens aboard the Revenge.
jory: Someone ought to go and look.

p5c4.begin.tutorial: Find the Grand Stenchmaster. (Jim saw him go below with a tablecloth and a pair of scissors.)
p5c4.begin.title: Dressed for Disaster

p5c4.hold: The hold is quiet. Too quiet. From somewhere behind the stacked crates in the far corner comes a sound you haven't heard since your grandmother's parlour.
Snip. Snip. The rasp of a needle through heavy cloth. Somebody, behind the crates, humming.

p5c4.hold.say: garrick[alarmed]: DON'T come any closer, Captain! You'll spoil it!
p5c4.hold.name: Garrick (behind the crates)

p5c4.hold.say: garrick[businesslike]: Assemble the crew on deck. All of them. I'll be up directly.
p5c4.hold.name: Garrick (behind the crates)

p5c4.hold: captain: Garrick, the starboard rail is being—

p5c4.hold.say: garrick[proud]: DIRECTLY, Captain! Genius can't be hurried! Mind the pins on your way out.
p5c4.hold.name: Garrick (behind the crates)

p5c4.hold.tutorial: Go back up on deck. (The crew are, apparently, to be assembled.)
p5c4.hold.title: Dressed for Disaster

p5c4.reveal: The crew stand about the main hatch in a ragged half-circle, poles in hand, glancing at the starboard rail every few seconds. The sharks can wait, apparently. Genius can't be hurried.
rook[annoyed]: How long's he going to be?
pete: He said directly.
rook: Directly WHAT?
A fanfare. From the hold. Nobody aboard owns a trumpet. Nobody can explain the fanfare. Several people step back from the hatch.
And up the ladder, slowly, one rung at a time, so that everyone gets the full effect, rises...

It is a coat. It is a CEREMONY of a coat. Burgundy and mustard, with facings in a green that has no business on clothes. It has epaulettes, and the epaulettes have epaulettes. The collar stands up past his ears like a pair of walls. Brass buttons the size of biscuits march down the front of it, and across his chest hang five medals, one of which is a bottle cap.
On his back, embroidered in yellow thread, a little cloud with three wiggly lines rising from it.
And over it all, sewn on now, stitched down along every edge so that it will never again come off: the sash.
garrick[proud]: Gentlemen. Captain. Behold: THE GRAND STENCHMASTER SUIT.
garrick[businesslike]: Allow me to walk you through it.
garrick[proud]: The SASH. Highest symbol of the office. Now permanently integrated. It must never, ever wrinkle.
pete: What happens if it wrinkles?
garrick[alarmed]: We don't talk about that.
garrick[proud]: The EPAULETTES. For atmospheric command.
gristle: What's atmospheric command?
garrick[businesslike]: Command. Of the atmosphere.
gristle: What does that MEAN, though?
garrick[smug]: It means epaulettes.
garrick[delighted]: And of course: the MEDALS.

p5c4.reveal.caption: Each one presented by the Grand Stenchmaster to the Grand Stenchmaster.

choice.text: The bottle cap (A Very Difficult Nap)

first: garrick[proud]: For surviving the first release. The big one. The treasure room.
captain: YOU did the first release.
garrick[businesslike]: And I survived it. Two achievements, one medal. Very efficient.
grog: garrick[proud]: For founding Frog Grog. A whole new beverage, Captain. Do you know how rarely that happens?
shark: garrick[proud]: For the first shark diversion. The rowboat. I was the bait. Very brave. Very fragrant.
jory: We LOWERED you. You screamed the whole way down.
forecast: garrick[proud]: For founding the Stench Forecasting service. In crayon. The highest scientific medium.
garrick[smug]: And not one complaint about accuracy.
nap: garrick[proud]: For completing a particularly difficult nap.
captain: How is a nap DIFFICULT?
garrick[businesslike]: It was during the frenzy, Captain. Very loud. Lot of screaming. I persevered.
captain: Why is it a bottle cap?
garrick[smug]: It was a very difficult nap. I had to improvise.

p5c4.tour_rest: garrick[proud]: The COAT. Odour-retentive ceremonial fabric. Holds a scent for weeks.
bob[surprised]: ...Why would you WANT it to hold a scent?
Garrick opens his mouth. Nothing comes out of it. He looks at Bob as though Bob has asked why the sea is wet.
garrick[offended]: ...I'm not going to dignify that.
garrick[proud]: And finally, the BOOTS. Reinforced, for high-pressure executive situations.
Everyone looks down at the boots. They are his ordinary boots, with bits of brass glued to them. One of the bits is a door hinge.
pete: Those are your boots with brass glued on.
garrick[businesslike]: Reinforcement.
gristle[annoyed]: We are LOSING the STARBOARD RAIL, and ye MADE a COSTUME?
garrick[offended]: Uniform.
pete[alarmed]: There are sharks biting holes through the hull!
garrick[businesslike]: Exactly. A Grand Stenchmaster must remain recognisable during emergencies.
bob[disgusted]: We already KNOW which one ye are!
garrick[smug]: Brand consistency.
Salty Jim has gone very quiet. He is looking hard at the lining of the coat, where it flaps open at the hem. It is white linen. It has a little embroidered anchor in one corner.
jim[surprised]: ...Did you use one of me GOOD tablecloths?
Garrick pauses.
jim[angry]: GARRICK.
garrick[nervous]: ...It was underutilised.
jim[angry]: UNDERUTILISED?! I've been saving that for CHRISTMAS!
Round the mainmast they go, Jim with a ladle and Garrick with his coat-tails flying, once, twice, and then Jim has to stop and put his hands on his knees.
garrick[smug]: Not a WRINKLE.
jim[angry]: I'll WRINKLE you.
And then, because you have to, you walk over and look at it properly.

You look at the boots. The brass. The coat. The buttons. The medals, and the bottle cap. The collar. The epaulettes on the epaulettes. The sash, stitched down for all eternity. The little embroidered cloud. Up, and up, and back down again.
captain[tired]: ...What... are ye wearing?
garrick[proud]: The STENCHMASTER SUIT.
captain: Take it off.
garrick[businesslike]: Impossible.
captain: Why?
garrick[proud]: Supreme duty. Every Grand Stenchmaster must wear the suit. With PRIDE.
rook[surprised]: ...Every Grand Stenchmaster?
garrick[businesslike]: Every one.
gristle[annoyed]: There has NEVER BEEN ANOTHER Grand Stenchmaster.
garrick[smug]: Well. Somebody has to establish the standards.
He brushes a speck off his epaulette, and the moment passes, and nobody thinks about it again.

p5c4.tour_rest.tutorial: Order the Grand Stenchmaster to help with the starboard rail.
p5c4.tour_rest.title: Dressed for Disaster

p5c4.order: CRACK. The starboard rail bows outward again. Somebody's bucket goes over the side.
captain[determined]: Garrick. If that suit stands for responsibility, prove it.
captain: Yes, near the water. That's where the sharks are.
garrick[alarmed]: With the SHARKS? In the ceremonial fabric? Captain, this is odour-retentive linen. One splash and it'll smell of SEA.
garrick[offended]: I can't risk the suit.
pete[alarmed]: YE MADE A SHARK-EMERGENCY UNIFORM THAT CANNOT GO NEAR SHARKS?!
gristle[annoyed]: Then why are ye WEARING it during SHARK DUTY?

p5c4.order.tutorial: Patch the three bites on the starboard rail (left-hand side). Stand at the rail beside each one, face it and press Confirm.
p5c4.order.title: Dressed for Disaster

p5c4.patch_a: A bite the size of a barrel lid, low down, splintered all round the edges.

p5c4.patch_a.text: I'm holding the MORALE, Mister Pete!

p5c4.patch_b: The stanchion here has been bitten nearly through. You lash it to the next one and nail a brace across.
p5c4.patch_c: A gap in the rail you could drive a cart through. A shark noses at it from below, hopefully.

p5c4.patch_c.text: Mind the one by the stern!

then: The starboard rail is whole again. Ugly, but whole. The crew stand back, dripping, splintered, shaking out their hands.
The Grand Stenchmaster, who has spent the entire repair standing in the middle of the deck adjusting his sash, sipping grog and waving graciously at the sharks, raises his mug.
garrick[delighted]: Splendid! Morale has never been HIGHER!
The crew look at him the way the sharks look at the hull.

p5.inspect.notes: Somebody has been pinning notes to the mainmast, near the Grand Stenchmaster's station. Nobody has seen who. Everybody has a crayon.

then.text: I've read them, you know. 'Nice costume.' It's a UNIFORM.
